tagline: A highway that made room for a creek.
intro: East of Zebulon, US 264 runs through Nash County pine and hardwood, with farmland showing between the trees, north of Middlesex and Bailey to the Wilson County line. It is 11 miles, about ten minutes.
The highway was moved onto this line in the 1970s. Planning it, the state widened the median rather than change Turkey Creek's channel, and the creek kept its own course between the lanes.

moments.title: Middlesex
moments.text: The highway passes north of town at the NC 231 interchange. The old US 264 through Middlesex was left behind as a business loop and now carries US 264 Alternate.

moments.title: Turkey Creek
moments.text: About 2,500 feet of the creek runs down the wide median, spared what the state guidebook calls a disastrous channel change.

sources.label: NCDOT, North Carolina Scenic Byways guidebook, Turkey Creek Byway
